# Bounded canonical boundary-label candidate

This candidate has not been generated or executed by its author. It is a local
untrusted adapter for the four frozen first proposals, not a source checker,
native acceptance rule, preservation theorem, adopted interpretation or std API.
The original eight native observations and unchanged requests remain evidence.

For widths 1–3, `generate.py` appends one canonical identity encoding, a positional
identity prefix and suffix rewire, and a composed enter sequence. It replaces
only the original entry definition, associated meaning and proof rows. The
resulting root is `[composed-enter, original-child-1, original-ordered-suffix…,
post]`. Every old nonroot row, reference and finite string's UTF-8 bytes is
retained; outer JSON whitespace is regenerated. Definition, meaning, proof and
encoding indices are resolved separately. Explicit child-cardinality and proof
associations, whole-table reachability and absence of other incoming root
references are checked. These local checks are not a semantic verifier.

Rewire arrays contain positions (`owners=[0]`, `axes=0..n-1`), never owner/axis
labels. The original output axis order and actual reversal remain unchanged in
the old body and suffix. Width 0 keeps the sole `Q<Bits<0>>` owner and the exact
single rewire body, permutation and proof: only its definition/meaning header
and sole identity encoding change owner label 101 to 0. No scalar or phase is
inserted. Requests are never rewritten and no mutants are prepared.

The two scripts reuse the frozen original capture guard, streaming helper and
forwarder. Each barrier retains the original 188-file packet, the previous
61-file candidate guard, all 233 FIRST source identities/inventories and observed
CLI/client/native file hashes. Maps compare data identity; only literal reviewed
code selects commands. Generation is one shot into
`canonical-label-preparation-01/`. Its ten generated data files receive
`prepared-files.json`; root must independently read/hash that map before capture.
Capture is one shot into `canonical-native-capture-01/`, exactly inspect then
unchanged request for each width, with fresh native results captured separately.
An unexpected rejection is retained rather than repaired. Success of the
recorder means completion of capture only.

The reused forwarder allows only the three frozen hierarchy mode/version pairs,
caps each input/output at 1 MiB and logs raw bytes, process argv and status.
Its intended stdin/native/grace budgets are `5 + 45 + 2 < 55` seconds; startup,
hashing and scheduling add overhead. The outer and native process groups differ;
an outer kill is not an assertion of killing every descendant. Missing inner
records remain operational uncertainty. File hashes do not attest compiled HEAD
or running-image identity.

After root and independent review of `canonical-inputs.json`, the fixed commands
are the following. `REVIEWED_DESIGN_SHA` is the observed candidate map hash;
`REVIEWED_PREPARED_SHA` must be observed after actual generation, not invented.

```sh
python3 tests/fixtures/frontend_v030/qft-exact-request-design/canonical-label-design-01/generate.py --design-map-sha256 REVIEWED_DESIGN_SHA
python3 tests/fixtures/frontend_v030/qft-exact-request-design/canonical-label-design-01/capture-adapted.py --client-sha256 683b29749f752652b3ddb8dba7fac0ea2d832f848178963f3056d2f5c03d8294 --design-map-sha256 REVIEWED_DESIGN_SHA --prepared-map-sha256 REVIEWED_PREPARED_SHA
```

No maximum-width run, general Fourier proof, whole-family integration,
constitutional guarantee, Issue completion or release/CI claim follows here.
